step_2_cardinality_cross_check.interpretation: The map is therefore scenario-scoped, not catalog-scoped: 535 entries is the right order of magnitude for the per-readout / per-participant fields emitted by one coupled roster fight, and is inconsistent with the leaf being a catalog listing. findings: Imperial Mandate (id 4005, tier 3, LEGENDARY, mode 'classic sr 5v5': true) — passive 'Command' (unique): immobilizing an enemy champion marks them Vulnerable for 4s, increasing damage they take FROM ALL SOURCES by 7%.

step_3_scenario_semantics_are_sourced.result: Both effects are 'from all sources' roster-wide amplifiers, so every participant's every damage source is in scope for this scenario. A per-entry {disposition, view_tag} map over hundreds of readout entries is structurally coherent for this scenario. Nothing about the two items' cached text is contradicted by the new leaf.

verdict_basis: Not-contradicted plus structural consistency, NOT an independent numeric recomputation. The leaf carries no quantity that cached wiki text or a math-foundations identity can determine: 'disposition' and 'view_tag' appear zero times in the entire evidence tree, and the payload is categorical (a status and a presentation tag), not a damage/stat number. Within what the evidence base can adjudicate: (a) the cardinality 535 matches no catalog enumeration in the cache, which is what one expects of a scenario-scoped readout manifest and rules out a mis-scoped catalog dump; (b) the scenario's two named items are both cached as 'from all sources' roster-wide amplifiers, so a per-entry map spanning the whole roster's damage sources is coherent; (c) math-foundations §4 states the engine's policy that unmodeled mechanics are disclosed, which an additive per-entry disposition map implements; (d) the old value is <absent>, which is not itself a computed value that could be 'correct' — it carried no information that the new map contradicts. No falsifier was found, so 'old_value_correct' and 'both_wrong' are both unsupported.
limitations: The oracle was not given the 535 entries themselves and is forbidden from reading scripts/golden_baseline.json, so individual disposition/view_tag values were NOT checked one by one. Only the leaf's existence, shape and cardinality were adjudicated.

This leaf is outside the oracle-verifiable domain defined by R-18/R-19 (recompute from cached wiki text or a quoted formula). If per-entry certification is required, it needs a different check — e.g. asserting the disposition vocabulary is closed and every entry's view_tag resolves to a declared view — which is a schema/invariant test, not a wiki-sourced recomputation.
A cardinality-only check cannot detect an off-by-a-few-entries error in the map (e.g. one participant's source omitted), because no source in data/ predicts the scenario's exact entry count.
